items.label: Aehr Test Systems press release: Aehr Receives $22 Million Follow-On Order for AI Processor (08-12-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Aehr received a $22 million follow-on production order from its lead wafer-level

set.signal: Aehr received a $22 million follow-on production order from its lead wafer-level AI processor customer (not named; described as a leading provider of advanced AI training and inference processors) for multiple fully automated FOX-XP wafer-level burn-in systems, each configured to test and burn in nine 300 mm wafers simultaneously, plus FOX WaferPak full-wafer contactors and integrated WaferPak Auto Aligners. Aehr expects to ship the systems over the next six months for installation at the customer's high-volume manufacturing partner in Taiwan. CEO Gayn Erickson: the customer's current production plans contemplate capacity beyond this order, and Aehr continues to engage with additional semiconductor companies and hyperscalers following positive wafer-level benchmark results; he believes the growing interest is driven in part by the increasing value and complexity of advanced AI packages combining processors, HBM, interface logic and other die, where screening for early-life failures before final assembly can deliver significant quality and economic benefits. Aehr says its WLBI systems reduce the risk of committing high-value HBM, substrates and interposers to devices that later fail reliability screening.

items.reason: Attribution: the HBM/substrate/interposer risk-avoidance point is in the company's (unquoted) release text, not the CEO quote; CEO quote says screening before final assembly 'can deliver significant quality and economic benefits'.
items.evidence: screening for early-life failures before final assembly can deliver significant quality and economic benefits.
